newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at an intra-day low of 8.3087 against U.S. on Wednesday, from Tuesday's 8.3072, on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.

Dealers said selling was triggered by the news in the official media on Wednesday that the People's Bank of China, the central bank, cut interest rates on reserves of commercial banks and other financial institutions deposited in the central bank.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.3070 and rose steadily to an intra-day high of 8.3062 in mid-session. It then fell quickly to 8.3080 before closing at a low.
Trading was active, with most done at 8.3065 and 8.3080, traders said.
"The cuts today were bad for the yuan, after reductions in deposit and loan interest rates last Friday," one dealer said.
This news means banks will pay less in interest to the central bank, he said.

Furthermore, the central bank is expected to cut the reserve rate of banks in the near future which implies a looser money policy, a second dealer said. "If such expectations prove true, the yuan will certainly fall due to lower demand," he said.
Dealers expect the yuan to consolidate around a bottom line of 8.3100 ahead of the weekend.
The yuan closed up at 7.6601 from 7.7100 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly down at 1.0735 from 1.0730 against the Hong Kong dollar.
